pr_title: Implement remaining unimplemented APIs for Builder types
pr_body:
- Implemented `DefineInitializedDataCore(...)`, `DefineUninitializedDataCore(...)`, `DefinePInvokeMethodCore(...)` for `TypeBuilerImpl`.
- Implemented `CreateGlobalFunctionsCore()`, `DefineGlobalMethodCore(...)`, `DefineInitializedDataCore(...)`, `DefineUninitializedDataCore(...)`, `DefinePInvokeMethodCore(...)`, `GetMethodImpl(...)`, `GetMethods()` for `ModuleBuilerImpl`.
- `requiredCustomModifiers`, `optionalCustomModifiers` for fields, method return type and parameters, which mostly involves Signature changes
- Had to refactor type/method/field token generation logic again because of global method/fields 
- Fix bugs found and [reported](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/96436)

Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/96436 and https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/97116
Contributes to https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/92975

issue_context.title: CheckInterfaces is too permissive and not permissive enough

review_comments: Why were the items reversed before?

Before the type tokens created on `TypeBuilder.CreateType()` and before saving the types are ordered with the token order, the types here created in inverse order, you can see that above on row 512-514. 

Now with a global type that has global methods/fields this ordering/token assignment not working anymore, now all types and its members tokens created before save (therefore in defined order no matter when `TypeBuilder.CreateType()` called)
Ideas on why this was TypeBuilder previously?
It was referenced internally to set the `TypeBuilder` of a generic method definition, to avoid casting I assume
Why was the use of remote executor changed?

Now using collectable ALC instead of default, the discussion is here https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/96805#discussion_r1448108301
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/e6d93336bd60870150cd9aad1c8c90fbe6fda496/src/libraries/System.Reflection.Emit/tests/PersistableAssemblyBuilder/AssemblySaveTools.cs#L12-L22
To make sure `requiredModifiers` has the `i`-th row
nit: whitespace off in the line above.
This is a bit sketchy, no? Are we sure users are going to know that calling this on the global type and no use the `null`?

There was a discussion about this https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/68840#issuecomment-1116726284, the global type only created internally (within `ModuleBuilder.CreateGlobalFunctions()`) and the returned null is not used.
